      Estimate(SystemInterface limitFluid, double temperature, double pressure, double sulfideLimit, double liquidLimit, double sulfideFugacity, double liquidFugacity, double mercuryFugacityCoefficient, double sulfideLimitLog10Uncertainty, double measured, double h2sFugacity, double h2sPpm, ReservoirMercuryEstimator.SulfidePhase sulfidePhase, ReservoirMercuryEstimator.HydrogenSulfideBasis hydrogenSulfideBasis, double mercurySulfideActivity, List<String> warnings)
      Creates an estimate.
      Parameters:
      limitFluid - fluid holding mercury at the controlling limit
      temperature - temperature [K]
      pressure - pressure [bara]
      sulfideLimit - mercury mole fraction at the sulfide limit
      liquidLimit - mercury mole fraction at the liquid mercury limit
      sulfideFugacity - mercury fugacity at the sulfide limit [bar]
      liquidFugacity - mercury fugacity at the liquid mercury limit [bar]
      mercuryFugacityCoefficient - fugacity coefficient of mercury at trace content in the first phase

      h2sPpm - H2S content used [ppm mol]

    • getSulfideSaturationIndex

      public double getSulfideSaturationIndex()
      Gets the saturation index of the given mercury content relative to the sulfide limit, log10(content / limit). Negative values mean the sulfide cannot hold the mercury back (supply-limited fluid); values near zero mean the fluid is at the sulfide limit; positive values mean supersaturation.
      Returns:
      saturation index, NaN if the fluid held no mercury

    • getLiquidSaturationIndex

      public double getLiquidSaturationIndex()
      Gets the saturation index of the given mercury content relative to liquid mercury, log10(content / limit). A positive value means free liquid mercury at reservoir conditions.
      Returns:
      saturation index, NaN if the fluid held no mercury

    • getApparentMercurySulfideActivity

      public double getApparentMercurySulfideActivity()
      Gets the mercury sulfide activity at which the given mercury content would be at equilibrium, a(HgS) x content / limit. For a fluid in equilibrium with mercury held in pyrite this is the HgS activity in the pyrite.
      Returns:
      apparent mercury sulfide activity, NaN if the fluid held no mercury
